headline: Chip Stocks Spearhead a Sweeping Monday Rally as 581 Names Climb
body_html:
Monday's session was a lopsided advance. Of the 665 stocks in our universe, 581 rose and only 84 fell. All nine sectors we track finished higher, and most did so by a wide margin, a sign that buyers were broadly engaged rather than clustered in a few corners.

Semiconductors led the rotation, up 7.9%, ahead of Financials at 5.94% and Industrials at 4.39%. Materials (3.31%) and Homebuilders (3.18%) followed, while Energy lagged with a 0.72% gain. Power-chip makers set the tone: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor surged 24.4% to take the top spot, and Monolithic Power added 16.67%. Optical and networking names joined in, with Coherent up 16.56% and Ubiquiti up 15.94%. Trade Desk gained 16.28% and Warby Parker 19.23%.

The damage was concentrated and stock-specific. Acadia Pharmaceuticals dropped 22.85%, Hims & Hers fell 12.19%, and several software platforms, including monday.com (down 8.91%) and Wix.com (down 8.03%), slid even as the software group rose 2.12%. With so few decliners, the real question for Tuesday is whether this appetite for risk holds or whether a day this one-sided invites some profit-taking.

briefs.headline: Boeing to Trim Commercial Jet Workforce
briefs.body: Boeing plans to cut about 5% of its commercial airplane workforce, saying its production ramp-up is moving more slowly than it had expected. The move shows how far output targets still lie from reality, even as industrials broadly rose on Monday.

briefs.headline: Children's Place Seeks Court Protection
briefs.body: The apparel retailer filed for bankruptcy protection and is looking for a buyer. The filing is a reminder that pressure on weaker consumer names persists, even on a day when the wider consumer group climbed 2.92%.

briefs.headline: Lilly Obesity Pill Shows Sleep Apnea Benefit
briefs.body: Eli Lilly reported that its experimental oral obesity treatment eased sleep apnea in a late-stage trial. The result is seen as clearing a path toward regulatory approval, and it adds to the growing list of conditions linked to weight-loss drugs.

briefs.headline: Goodyear Chief Steps Aside Mid-Turnaround
briefs.body: Goodyear Tire's chief executive, Mark Stewart, is stepping down while the company is still working through its turnaround plan. Leadership changes partway through a restructuring tend to draw close scrutiny from investors.

briefs.headline: Housing Supply Builds, Sellers Hold Firm
briefs.body: Home listings piled up in October, yet sellers are showing little willingness to cut asking prices. That standoff between supply and pricing is the backdrop for a homebuilder group that gained 3.18% on the session.

briefs.headline: Iran Peace Talks Show No Imminent Breakthrough
briefs.body: President Trump is set to meet Qatar, which is mediating in the Iran war, but no deal looks close. Tehran defended its short proposal for talks after Washington rejected its conditions. Energy was Monday's weakest sector, up just 0.72%.
